q: Sec. 27.2 requires a PCA to obtain what, scaled to the magnitude and scope of his project involvement?
o: Professional liability insurance or a bond
A business permit for each project
n: Sec. 27.2 requires the PCA to secure a Professional Liability Insurance Policy, professional indemnity insurance, or an equivalent bond, commensurate with the project's magnitude, scope, and corresponding compensation; its cost forms part of the total project cost chargeable to the Client. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 27.2)

q: Under Sec. 19.10, which item counts as a Direct Cost/Reimbursable Expense rather than Overhead?
o: Office rent and air-conditioning for the workspace
Identifiable long-distance telephone, internet, and courier/postage expenses tied directly to the project
Executive and administrative salaries that can't be tied to a specific project
General business development expenses of the firm
n: Sec. 19.10.2 lists identifiable communication expenses (long-distance telephone, telegraph, internet, SMS, cable, express charge, postage) as Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses, distinct from Overhead items like office space, general administrative salaries, and business development expenses (Sec. 19.14). (Source: SPP Document 209, Secs. 19.10.2, 19.14)

q: Per Sec. 23, in what manner may a PCA render PACS to the Client?
o: Only via an accredited foreign partner
Only directly, never through a firm
As the Commission/Board prescribes via IAPOA
n: Sec. 23 provides that a PCA may provide services directly or indirectly to the Client, in the manner prescribed, suggested, or promulgated by the Commission/Board through the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 23)

q: What consequence does Sec. 30 impose on someone practicing PACS without the qualifications R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR require?
o: Sanctions, plus possible criminal or civil cases
n: Sec. 30 provides that anyone who engages in PACS without the qualifications prescribed under R.A. No. 9266 and its IRR shall be subject to sanction/s by appropriate public or private entities, without prejudice to filing criminal, civil, administrative or special complaints. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 30)

q: Per Sec. 19.12, an FC/FA's temporary/special permit (TSP) must implement which R.A. No. 9266 sections?
n: Sec. 19.12.2 requires the FC/FA to have acquired a temporary/special permit (TSP) to practice architecture on Philippine soil in accordance with Board Resolutions implementing Secs. 37 and 38 of R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.12.2)

q: For what kind of engagement does Sec. 24.7.1's Per Diem or Hourly Basis method fit best?
o: Projects whose cost cannot be estimated
n: Sec. 24.7.1 states the Per Diem or Hourly Basis method suits engagements involving intermittent personal service, compensating the PCA for all time devoted to the work, including travel time, plus reimbursement of related out-of-pocket expenses. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.1)

q: How does SPP Document 209 fit alongside the other issuances governing architectural practice?
o: It applies only to foreign consultants
It complements RA 9266 and other laws
n: Sec. 16.8 clarifies that the SPP on PACS is meant to complement existing PRLs, the IP Code, the GPRA, the CES and other SPPs, and that nothing in it must unduly affect those laws, policies, rules, regulations, the CES, and other SPPs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.8)

q: What factors does Sec. 19.13 say drive variation in the PACS fee "multiplier"?
o: Type of work, organization and office location
n: Sec. 19.13 states the multiplier varies according to the types of architectural consulting work, the PCA's organization and experience, and the geographic area where the office is located. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.13)

q: Which Sec. 24.7.4 sub-method is defined as building a fixed compensation figure directly, by estimating each cost-outline element and adding a reasonable profit margin?
o: The Percentage of Total Project Cost method (Sec. 24.7.5)
n: Sec. 24.7.4(b) describes direct development of a fixed lump-sum amount by estimating individual cost-outline elements plus a reasonable profit margin, as distinct from sub-method (a), which computes the lump sum as a percentage of estimated total project cost. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4(b))

q: After LoI No. 1000, which pair of organizations first put together the original Standard Guidelines on Consultancy/Consulting Services?
n: The PFPA (umbrella organization of PRC-accredited professional associations) and the PTC (then composed of 14 accredited technological APOs) initiated the original guidelines document. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.2)

q: For PACS purposes specifically, what does Sec. 19.16 say the term "Accredited Professional Organization (APO)" designates?
o: The Philippine Federation of Professional Associations (PFPA)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Sec. 19.16 states that while APO generally covers organizations under the CBNE/PTC umbrella, for PACS purposes the term specifically refers to the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.16)

q: How does Sec. 24.8 say fees for artistic, innovative, and creative work should be set, relative to purely technical/scientific work?
o: In exactly the same way as fees for purely technical and scientific work
Always at a lower rate than technical services
Only through the Per Diem/Hourly method
Differently from how fees for purely technical and scientific undertakings are set
n: Sec. 24.8 states that fees for artistic, innovative and creative services shall not be determined in the same manner as fees for purely technical and scientific undertakings. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.8)

q: What does SPP Document 209 identify as its primary purpose?
n: Sec. 16.8 states the SPP's primary purpose is to complement R.A. No. 9266, the IP Code (R.A. 8293), the GPRA (R.A. 9184), the CES, other SPPs, and related regulations, and that nothing in it must unduly affect those laws and issuances. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.8)

q: Beyond chargeable salaries (sick leave, vacation, holiday, and incentive pay included), what else does Sec. 19.20 fold into "Salary Cost"?
o: Payroll taxes and social security contributions
n: Sec. 19.20 defines Salary Cost as including chargeable salaries plus excise/payroll and other imposable taxes/duties and contributions for social security and insurance benefits. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.20)

q: Given the situation above, which Sec. 24.7 compensation method fits best, and for what reason?
o: Per Diem or Hourly Basis, since it is the only method that reimburses travel expenses
Retainer, since the firm expects to remain on call over a long stretch of time
Salary Cost times a Multiplier, plus Direct Cost/Reimbursable Expenses, since this suits projects whose costs are hard to fix in advance and where investigative work could still change the scope
Percentage of Total Project Cost, since it is the simplest method to apply to any project
n: Sec. 24.7.3 states the Salary Cost x Multiplier + Direct Cost method is best suited for projects for which costs are difficult to pre-determine, or where additional investigative work may further alter the project's scope — exactly the scenario described. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3)
scenario: A Registered Architectural Firm (RAF) puts a five-person team of PCAs and support staff on a mixed-use development where costs are hard to fix in advance, and further investigative work could still reshape the project's scope. The team's chargeable basic Salary Cost for the project comes to PHP 500,000, while the firm's Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses for the engagement total PHP 150,000.

q: Sec. 17.1's Objectives name what basic legal precondition someone must meet before becoming a PCA?
o: Membership in a foreign professional institute
An employee of a government agency
Holding a master's degree in architecture
Being a registered and licensed Architect (RLA)
n: Sec. 17.1 states that by law, PCAs must first be registered and licensed Architects (RLAs), on which basis standards are built to develop their competencies, credibility and integrity. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 17.1)

q: Which activity does Sec. 20 count within PACS's scope?
n: Sec. 20.4 explicitly lists teaching, lecturing, coaching, mentoring as within the scope of PACS. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.4)

q: Given the situation, what must the lump-sum agreement additionally spell out besides the fee itself, per Sec. 24.7.4?
o: A time limit and pay for extra time
A switch to per diem after a year
A waiver of the PCA's seal
n: Sec. 24.7.4 requires lump-sum agreements to contain a clearly stated time limit for the services and a provision for additional compensation for extra time used, plus clarity on where final approval authority lies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4)
scenario: For a residential subdivision project whose PACS scope can be fully spelled out from the start, an Owner engages a PCA. They agree to compute the fee under Sec. 24.7.4(a) of SPP Document 209 — a lump sum set as a percentage of the estimated total project cost — pegging the rate at 6% of an estimated total project cost of PHP 20,000,000.

q: Sec. 18.2 characterizes RLPs' (such as RLAs') adherence to their respective SPPs as what?
o: Waivable upon a written request to the Commission
n: Sec. 18.2 states it "shall be mandatory" upon all RLPs, such as RLAs, to strictly adhere to their respective SPPs within the bounds of their profession's scope of practice. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 18.2)

q: Besides SEC or DTI registration, what must a juridical-person PCA (consulting firm) also hold, per Sec. 21.2?
o: A minimum paid-up capital of PHP 10,000,000
A separate license from the Department of Foreign Affairs
A certificate of good standing from a foreign chamber of commerce
A valid Commission certificate to operate as a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF)
n: Sec. 21.2 requires the consulting firm, in addition to SEC/DTI registration, to possess a valid Commission certificate to operate as a Registered Architectural Firm (RAF). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.2)

q: Per Sec. 26, what is needed before a PCA's architectural documents can be duplicated or copied for use on another or repeat project?
o: The written consent of the PCA or the documents' author
No consent at all, so long as the Client paid for the original project
Only the Commission's approval, bypassing the PCA's consent
A separate government copyright registration for every instance
n: Sec. 26 provides that no person, without the written consent of the PCA/author, shall duplicate or copy such documents for use in repetition of, or for other, projects, whether executed partly or in entirety. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 26)

q: How does SPP Document 209 define a "Consulting Agreement"?
o: A binding contract between PCA and Client on terms
n: Sec. 19.6 defines a Consulting Agreement as a binding covenant or understanding between a PCA and/or consulting firm (RAF) and an Owner/Client that sets out mutually agreed terms and conditions under which the specific work requiring special/technical skills shall be undertaken. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.6)

q: When a developer must turn to a foreign architect for a CBNE specialization because no qualified FPCA exists in that field, what else does Sec. 22.2 require?
o: Nothing further, once it's shown no FPCA is available
Taking on at least ten (10) Filipino architects as understudies
Employing at least two (2) Filipino RLAs in that same specialization as understudies
Securing written approval from the President of the Philippines
n: Sec. 22.2 provides that where no qualified FPCA is available and a non-FPCA (FA/FC) is engaged, a minimum of two (2) Filipino RLAs in the same field of specialization shall be employed as understudies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.2)

q: Per Sec. 28, once the IAPOA adopts this SPP for PACS, what must it go on to formulate?
o: An amendment to the National Building Code
A new law meant to supersede R.A. No. 9266
A separate licensure examination for PACS practitioners
The covering guidelines and Manual of Procedure (MoP)
n: Sec. 28 states this SPP shall be adopted by the IAPOA, which shall thereafter formulate the covering guidelines and Manual of Procedure (MoP). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 28)

q: What status does an FPCA acquire the moment he signs and seals architectural documents?
n: Sec. 19.11 states that if the FPCA signs and seals architectural documents, he becomes an Architect-of-record (AOR) for the project and assumes the attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.11)

q: Sec. 24.2 says compensation for PACS needing more than one type of expertise should be handled how, relative to PACS needing only a single kind?
o: Differently — single/related-expertise PACS is treated differently from multi-expertise PACS
It must always be paid at a lower rate than single-expertise PACS
It cannot be compensated at all under this SPP
n: Sec. 24.2 states that compensation for PACS requiring only one kind of expertise (or related types) shall be treated differently from those requiring more than one type of expertise. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.2)

q: On 27 July 2010, SPP Document 209 was approved as a supplemental IRR of what law?
n: The footer of every page of SPP Document 209 (part of the 2010 Standards of Professional Practice) states it was "Approved 27 July 2010 as the Supplemental IRR of R.A. No. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004)." (Source: SPP Document 209, page footer)

q: Among its requirements, Sec. 19.12 says an FC must be what?
o: A licensed architect in his own country
n: Sec. 19.12.4 requires the FC/FA to be a registered and/or licensed professional architect in his own country of origin (and/or country of residence/practice). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.12.4)

q: When does Sec. 24.7.2's Retainer method of payment come into play?
o: For services at intervals, to assure availability
When cost can never be estimated
n: Sec. 24.7.2 explains the Retainer method is used when the PCA's services are expected to be required at intervals over time, ensuring in advance that his services will be available to the Client when required. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.2)

q: Which older document does SPP Document 209 officially supersede?
n: The title page of SPP Document 209 states it is "(replacing the 1981 UAP Doc. 210)." (Source: SPP Document 209, title page)

q: Which of these does Sec. 19.14 classify as Overhead, rather than a project's Direct Cost/Reimbursable Expense?
o: Special consultants' fees directly applicable to the contracted work
Blue-printing and reproduction costs for the work
Depreciation allowances or rental of the office's furniture, equipment, and instruments
Long-distance telephone charges tied to the project
n: Sec. 19.14.2 classifies depreciation allowances or rental of office furniture, equipment and instruments as Overhead, distinct from the project-specific Direct Costs listed under Sec. 19.10. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.14.2)

q: For a lump-sum compensation arrangement, Sec. 24.7.4 says the agreement must clearly spell out what?
o: That the fee is payable only upon project completion, with no interim payments
That no time limit ever governs lump-sum agreements
That the PCA waives any right to additional compensation no matter how the scope changes
A time limit for performing the services, plus a provision for additional compensation for extra time used
n: Sec. 24.7.4 states lump-sum agreements should contain a clearly stated time limit for performing the services, with provision for additional compensation for extra time used, and clarity on where final design-approval authority lies. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4)

q: Under a Joint Resolution dated December 11, 2009, the PTC co-drafted the amended 2010 Standard Guidelines together with which body?
o: The Council for the Built and Natural Environments (CBNE)
The Integrated and Accredited Professional Organization of Architects (IAPOA)
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: The amended version is based on the document jointly drafted by the PTC and the Council for the Built and Natural Environments (CBNE), per their Joint Resolution No. 2009-01 dated December 11, 2009. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.5)

q: How does Sec. 19.17 define "PACS" as rendered by a PCA or consulting firm (RAF)?
o: The sale of plans to the public
n: Sec. 19.17 defines PACS as the rendering by a PCA or a consulting firm (RAF) of independent advice, technical assistance/services, and activities requiring appropriate knowledge, skills, training, experience, recognized competence, integrity, and/or financial and logistical capability. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.17)

q: Per Sec. 24.9, who promulgates, approves, and adopts the criteria for setting PACS compensation methods?
o: The Department of Budget and Management
n: Sec. 24.9 states the criteria for establishing method/s of compensation shall be promulgated, approved and adopted by the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.9)

q: The Rationale argues that fully using Filipino Professional Consultants (FPCs) chiefly benefits the country in what way?
o: Less importing of foreign expertise and currency
n: Sec. 16.4 states that full utilization of FPCs can minimize the importation of foreign expertise, which entails considerable expenditure of hard-earned foreign exchange. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.4)

q: Whose charter, by-laws, and rules — channeled through which body — determine the scope of PACS under Sec. 20?
o: The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
n: Sec. 20 states the scope of PACS is defined per the charter, by-laws, policies, rules and regulations of the Commission and the Board through the IAPOA to which the PCA belongs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20)

q: Applying Sec. 24.7.3's formula (Fee = Salary Cost × Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses) with the SPP's 3.0 multiplier factor, what total fee results from the scenario above?
n: Fee = (PHP 500,000 x 3.0) + PHP 150,000 = PHP 1,500,000 + PHP 150,000 = PHP 1,650,000. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3 (formula: Fee = Salary Cost x Multiplier + Reimbursable Expenses; multiplier factor of 3.0))
scenario: A Registered Architectural Firm (RAF) puts a five-person team of PCAs and support staff on a mixed-use development where costs are hard to fix in advance, and further investigative work could still reshape the project's scope. The team's chargeable basic Salary Cost for the project comes to PHP 500,000, while the firm's Direct Costs/Reimbursable Expenses for the engagement total PHP 150,000.

q: Sec. 17.3 lists compliance with advisories on engaging foreign architects/consultants as an Objective, meant to achieve what?
o: A fair field for Filipino consultants
n: Sec. 17.3 aims at full compliance with guidelines on engaging foreign architects/consultants as a measure to stimulate the local market for RLA-PCAs and protect/level the field between RLAs and FAs/FCs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 17.3)

q: What is the final item listed under Sec. 20.16 within PACS's scope?
o: Site selection, analysis, evaluation, ranking, and development
Land use and multi-sectoral development planning
n: Sec. 20.16, the final item in the Sec. 20 enumeration, is "Capital Investment Programming." (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.16)

q: Under Sec. 25, a PCA may sign and seal his architectural documents and deliverables only under what condition?
o: Only if he is also the Architect-of-record
Only if the Client asks in writing
n: Sec. 25 conditions the sealing of documents on the PCA also acting as Architect-of-record (Aor), in which case he assumes all attendant professional responsibilities and civil liabilities for the project. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 25)

q: How does SPP Document 209 define "Comprehensive Development"?
n: Sec. 19.1 defines Comprehensive Development as the holistic and progressive growth of a community, province, region and nation, inclusive of its economic, social, physical, environmental and institutional sectors. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.1)

q: Sec. 21.5 requires a PCA to meet what qualification?
o: At least fifty years of age
n: Sec. 21.5 requires that the PCA has never been convicted of any criminal or administrative offense related to deliberate wrongdoing. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.5)

q: How does Sec. 27.1 describe the liability of any individual, partner, firm, or joint venture engaged in PACS?
o: Responsible to the State; civilly liable to all
n: Sec. 27.1 states that anyone engaged in PACS is legally/professionally responsible before the State and civilly liable before the State, the general public, and the Client, for the conduct and performance of services rendered. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 27.1)

q: Beyond the Commission/Board, with which agency must a Consulting Architectural Firm (CAF) be registered, per Sec. 19.7?
o: SEC, or DTI if a sole proprietorship
n: Sec. 19.7 defines a CAF as a corporation/association/group/partnership registered with the SEC, or a sole proprietorship registered with the DTI, and likewise registered with the Commission/Board. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.7)

q: Sec. 22.3 ties the selection of PCAs for Government projects to which law's relevant provisions?
o: R.A. No. 9184 (the Government Procurement Reform Act of 2003)
R.A. No. 9266 alone, without reference to procurement law
n: Sec. 22.3 requires that selection of PCAs for Government projects follow the relevant provisions of R.A. No. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act (GPRA) of 2003. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.3) RA 9184 was repealed by RA 12009, the New Government Procurement Act, in force since 13 August 2024, though the SPP still cites RA 9184.

q: Which ADR modes, mandated by R.A. No. 9285, must Sec. 29 necessarily cover for disputes over the IRR's implementation?
o: Arbitration only, to the exclusion of every other mode
An administrative complaint before the PRC, exclusively
n: Sec. 29 requires that ADR modes under R.A. No. 9285 (the ADR Act of 2004) be used before referral to a competent court, and that these must necessarily include negotiation, conciliation, mediation and arbitration; an ADR clause must form part of all PACS agreements. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 29)

q: Beyond citizenship and being a natural person, Sec. 19.11 requires an FPCA to also be what?
o: A holder of a foreign license
A graduate of a foreign school
A Philippine RLA in good IAPOA standing
n: Sec. 19.11 requires the FPCA to be a Philippine-registered and licensed architect (RLA), a member in good standing of the IAPOA, and specializing in a State-regulated branch of architecture under R.A. No. 9266. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.11)

q: For identical scopes of work, what does Sec. 24.4 require regarding compensation between FPCAs and their FC counterparts?
o: That there be no disparity between the two
That it be left entirely to informal negotiation, with no guiding principle
That FPCAs always be favored by a fixed multiplier
That FCs always be favored by at least 20%
n: Sec. 24.4 explicitly states there shall be no disparity in compensation between FPCAs and their FC counterparts for the same scope of work. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.4)

q: Under SPP Document 209, who is authorized to render PACS?
o: A foreigner on a tourist visa
A PCA or registered architectural firm
n: Throughout SPP Document 209 (Secs. 19.11, 19.15, 19.17, 21), PACS is rendered by qualified PCAs (natural persons who are RLAs and IAPOA members in good standing) or by RAFs (juridical persons meeting SEC/DTI and Commission requirements), including FPCAs. (Source: SPP Document 209, Secs. 19.11, 19.15, 19.17, 21)

q: Sec. 19.13's "Multiplier" covers the PCA for all of the following except which one?
o: Fee for contingencies, interest on capital reserves, and profit
The direct construction cost of the project
n: Sec. 19.13 lists the multiplier's components as overhead costs, fringe benefits/social charges, fee for contingencies, interest on capital reserves, and profit — not the direct construction cost of the project. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.13)

q: Sec. 24.7.3 says the "Salary Cost times Multiplier, plus Direct Cost" method suits projects with what characteristic?
o: A total project cost that's already fixed and fully known in advance
Only personal services eligible for per diem payment
A Client insisting on a lump-sum fee no matter how the scope changes
Costs that are hard to predetermine, or where added experimental/investigative work could still reshape the scope
n: Sec. 24.7.3 states this method is best suited for projects whose costs are difficult to pre-determine, or where additional experimental or investigative work may be needed that could further alter the project's scope. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.3)

q: Who issued LoI No. 1000 on March 20, 1980, and what did it direct?
n: LoI No. 1000 was issued by then-President Ferdinand E. Marcos, directing all government agencies and instrumentalities to give priority to members of accredited professional organizations (APOs) in hiring and in engaging professional services. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.1)

q: Sec. 19.15 requires a PCA to hold what, among other things?
o: A postgraduate degree from a foreign university
A valid registration certification and Commission ID card, plus good standing in the IAPOA
A business permit from the local government unit, and nothing else
n: Sec. 19.15 requires the PCA to be a Philippine-registered and licensed Architect (RLA) with a valid registration certification and Commission ID card, and a member in good standing of the IAPOA. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.15)

q: On what assumption does Sec. 24.7.5 say the validity of the 'Percentage of Total Project Cost' method depends?
o: The rate must exceed 20% of cost
Only government projects may use it
Costs vary in proportion to project cost
Costs are fixed regardless of cost
n: Sec. 24.7.5 states the method's validity rests on the assumption that consultancy costs vary in proportion to total project cost, regardless of project type or location, and should be applied only where experience shows an approximate correlation. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.5)

q: According to the Foreword, what triggered the 2010 review of the original 1981 guidelines?
o: A PRBoA order to renumber SPPs
A wave of foreign and unqualified "consultants"
n: The Foreword explains that three decades after 1981, it became urgent to revisit the document because of the influx of foreign consultants and the rise of entities projecting themselves as "consultants" without adequate skills, training or experience. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 15.4)

q: Sec. 19.18 defines "Project Cost" as covering, but not limited to, which of these?
o: Construction, fees, land and related costs
n: Sec. 19.18 defines Project Cost as the total project cost including but not limited to construction cost, professional fees, cost of land/ROW, and legal, administrative and other related client expenses. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.18)

q: Barring a different mutual agreement, when does a PCA's entitlement to BSP-rate-plus-IAPOA-percentage interest on unpaid fees kick in, under Sec. 24.10?
o: Thirty days after receipt of the billing
Immediately upon any billing being issued, with no grace period
Ninety days after the contract is signed
n: Sec. 24.10 grants the PCA interest at the BSP prevailing rate plus an IAPOA-determined percentage on fees, other charges, and reimbursements not paid within 30 days from receipt of billing, unless otherwise mutually agreed. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.10)

q: Per the Rationale in Sec. 16.5, why is the presence of foreign architects in the Philippines seen as problematic?
o: They are exempt from Philippine tax
Their "technology transfer" is local; they displace RLPs
They are barred from practicing here
n: Sec. 16.5 explains that the technology foreign consultants claim to transfer is often already available in adequate proportion locally, so their presence instead displaces Filipino Professional Consultants (FPCs) from significant projects. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 16.5)

q: Which item does Sec. 20 explicitly place within the scope of PACS?
n: Sec. 20.7 lists "conduct of pre-investment/pre-feasibility and feasibility studies" among the scope items of PACS. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 20.7)

q: Applying Sec. 24.7.4(a)'s percentage-of-project-cost approach to the scenario above, what lump-sum fee results?
n: Lump-sum fee = 6% x PHP 20,000,000 = PHP 1,200,000, computed as a percentage of the estimated total project cost per Sec. 24.7.4(a). (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 24.7.4(a))
scenario: For a residential subdivision project whose PACS scope can be fully spelled out from the start, an Owner engages a PCA. They agree to compute the fee under Sec. 24.7.4(a) of SPP Document 209 — a lump sum set as a percentage of the estimated total project cost — pegging the rate at 6% of an estimated total project cost of PHP 20,000,000.

q: Quoting Sec. 14, Art. XII of the 1987 Constitution, what does SPP Document 209's Declaration of Policy say about the practice of professions in the Philippines?
o: That a uniform national licensing fee applies regardless of profession
That it is limited to Filipino citizens, save in cases prescribed by law
That it is regulated solely by private professional associations
That it is open to any foreign national holding a work visa
n: Sec. 18.1 quotes Sec. 14, Art. XII of the 1987 Constitution: "The practice of all professions in the Philippines shall be limited to Filipino citizens, save in cases prescribed by law." (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 18.1 (1987 Constitution, Art. XII, Sec. 14))

q: For a natural-person PCA, what must he/she be under Sec. 21.1?
o: A lawyer who passed the bar
A Filipino RLA with a valid ID, IAPOA member
A holder of a foreign license only
n: Sec. 21.1 requires the natural-person PCA to be a Filipino citizen who is a duly registered and licensed Architect, holding a valid Commission ID card-license and IAPOA good standing. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 21.1)

q: Sec. 26 protects a PCA's architectural documentary outputs under which R.A. No. 9266 provisions?
n: Sec. 26 states such outputs and materials are protected under Secs. 20(4) and 33 of R.A. No. 9266 and its 2004 IRR, whether executed or not. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 26)

q: How does Sec. 19.2 define a "Consortium or Association"?
o: Filipino consultants, alone or with foreign ones
n: Sec. 19.2 defines Consortium or Association as a coalition of purely Filipino RLA-PCAs/RAFs, or such Filipino consultants/firms in collaboration with foreign consultants/firms authorized to render consulting services. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 19.2)

q: Sec. 22.1 names what as the major consideration in hiring a PCA?
n: Sec. 22.1 states the major consideration in hiring a PCA is his/her qualifications as provided in the SPP — competence, capabilities and integrity. (Source: SPP Document 209, Sec. 22.1)
